verdict.rationale: Ardent's docs say it creates instant, isolated copies of a production Postgres database from the CLI (`ardent branch create`). The copies include real data, and clones load in about 6s without duplicating storage, which implies copy-on-write semantics. Per-PR branches and destructive testing against an exact production copy are documented directly. missing for 10: explicit statement of the copy-on-write mechanism (only implied by 'do not duplicate storage'), independent hands-on corroboration of instant branching speed (especially on large databases).

support.subject: As a developer, I can create an instant copy-on-write branch of my database — schema and data — to develop and test against production-shaped data

citations.quote: Ardent creates instant, isolated copies of your production Postgres database — in seconds, right from your terminal.
Clones load in 6s, scale to 0, autoscale compute and do not duplicate storage.
Ardent lets you run your full test suite, including destructive operations, against an exact copy of production.
Test migrations, run schema changes, and let coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor actually verify their database work — all against real data, without touching production.
